perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith is a construction worker; Elizabeth Sun is a receptionist at the same construction company. They are colleagues with a friendly, professional relationship, often interacting when Keith comes to the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him over several days. He wondered if he had unknowingly upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- Keith understood her shortness was not caused by anger toward him but by personal stress. He felt sympathetic.
- He offered to listen/talk and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith told her he appreciated her sharing and suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure/hesitant about seeking help.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn after this. He thought he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he wanted her to know he supported her no matter what. Elizabeth said he had not overstepped, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Afterward, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him. He intends to maintain a supportive relationship.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
